Each layer keeps its own ordered list of migration files. An admin applies the pending files from the admin UI.

## How it works

- A layer keeps its migrations in `db/migrations/`, as `001_baseline.sql`, `002_admin_hardening.sql`, and so on.
- The table `public.pluto_migrations` records one row for each applied file. The ledger key of `@plutocms/supabase` is `core`. The other layers use their package name without the scope.
- When `DATABASE_URL` is set, the server also applies the pending files of every layer when it starts.
- In development, after the server applies a new file, it regenerates `shared/types/supabase.ts` from the live schema.
- A banner in the admin tells you when a layer has pending migrations. **Go to Migrations** opens `/admin/migrations`.
- The page lists the pending layers and the applied layers.

## Run the migrations

`POST /api/migrations/run` applies every pending migration file across the layers. Only an admin can call it. The route checks `profiles.is_admin` directly, so it needs no migration to work.

### Connection string

The route picks the connection string in this order:

1. `process.env.DATABASE_URL`, if it is set. A string in the request body is then ignored.
2. Otherwise, the `connectionString` in the request body.
3. Otherwise, the answer is `{ success: false, needsConnectionString: true }`.

Rule 1 is the security model of the route. It stops an admin from pointing the server at another database host.

After a successful run, the server writes `DATABASE_URL` to `.env`. If the write fails, the migrations still succeed. The response reports `persisted: false`, and the page shows a step-by-step manual fix with the `DATABASE_URL="..."` line to copy.

::note
The server never returns the connection string and never logs it. Error messages are scrubbed of the connection string and the password.
::

## Per-file transactions

The runner applies each file on its own.

- All statements of a file run in one transaction, together with the ledger row.
- If a statement fails, the whole file rolls back. Nothing from it is applied.
- A failure in one file stops the rest of that layer, because a later file often depends on an earlier one. Those files report `Skipped: an earlier migration in this layer failed.`
- A failure never blocks another layer. Each layer runs on its own.

### Files that cannot run in a transaction

A statement such as `create index concurrently` cannot run in a transaction. Make `-- pluto:no-transaction` the first non-blank line of the file. The runner then runs the statements one at a time and records the ledger row after. A failure can leave the file partly applied, so write such a file with `if not exists` and `on conflict` guards.

## Checksums

The runner records a checksum for each file (the first 16 hex characters of a SHA-256 digest). On a later boot, if an applied file has a different checksum, the runner logs a warning with the layer and the file name. It does not fail and does not run the file again. This warns you that someone edited a shipped migration.

## Write a migration

Add a new file to `db/migrations/` of your layer.

- Name it `NNN_slug.sql`. `NNN` is the next zero-padded number.
- Never edit a file that has shipped or that any database has applied.
- Never renumber a file. The number is part of its identity in the ledger.
- `001_baseline.sql` is a reserved name. Do not reuse it.
- Write the file so it is safe to run on a database that has every earlier file applied.
- Use `if not exists`, `on conflict`, and `drop ... if exists` guards where they make sense.
- A migration that creates a table must grant it. See [Data API grants](/supabase/grants).

## Dev server restart

In development, writing `.env` restarts the Nuxt dev server. The HTTP response can be cut off even when the migration succeeded. In this case, the page shows a "reconnecting" toast. It checks the server every two seconds, for up to thirty seconds.

## Migrations in the shipped layers

| Layer | Files |
| --- | --- |
| `supabase` | `001_baseline`, `002_admin_hardening`, `003_settings_generic_keys`, `004_roles_and_capabilities`, `005_profile_locale`, `006_data_api_grants`, `007_restrict_staff_reads`, `008_users_and_roles_admin` |
| `supabase-shop` | `001_baseline`, `002_admin_policies`, `003_capability_policies`, `004_price_in_cents`, `005_data_api_grants` |
| `supabase-blog` | `001_baseline`, `002_admin_policies`, `003_capability_policies`, `004_data_api_grants` |
| `supabase-storage` | `001_baseline`, `002_media_decouple_and_admin`, `003_capability_policies`, `004_media_backfill_storage_path`, `005_data_api_grants` |
